method: Same-agent English/Marathi close reading, quantifier and conditional-scope inspection, formula/token comparison and reverse paraphrase with checked native terminology; not independent or human review.
scope: Satisfiable, unsatisfiable, tautological and contingent formulas; semantic entailment; basic entailment laws; unsatisfiability and the semantic deduction theorem.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: A formula is satisfiable when some valuation satisfies it and unsatisfiable when none does; it is a tautology when every valuation satisfies it and contingent when satisfiable but not tautological. Gamma entails A exactly when every valuation satisfying Gamma satisfies A. A set is satisfiable exactly when some valuation satisfies all of it.
samples.checks: Existential, universal and negative quantifier scopes are distinct; the entailment direction and the set-level satisfaction condition are unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The exercise asks, for each of four unchanged formulas, whether it is satisfiable, a tautology and contingent.
samples.checks: All four formulas, their order and all three requested classifications are preserved exactly.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Tautologicity is entailment from the empty set; semantic modus ponens holds; satisfiability descends to finite subsets; entailment is monotone under enlarging premises; and the stated transitivity/cut principle combines Gamma and Delta.
samples.checks: Every premise set, subset direction, union, conditional and conclusion remains attached to the same formula as in the source.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Gamma entails A exactly when Gamma together with not-A is unsatisfiable. Gamma entails A implies B exactly when Gamma together with A entails B.
samples.checks: Both biconditional directions, negation scope, conditional scope and premise-set extensions are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Each stated result is left as an exercise and each following problem points to the same proposition or theorem label.
samples.checks: All proof placeholders and cross-reference identifiers are unchanged.

limitations: No independent linguistic review has been performed.
